takeaway: Tropical wave day. The wave is crossing Costa Rica today, earlier than the 'Saturday night' timing in yesterday's outlook. Expect a few showers possible before noon, then stronger storms this afternoon and evening, with rain lingering on the North Pacific tonight. Costa Rica's weather service has an alert out and flags already-soaked soils in Guanacaste. Nicoya tops out near 34°C. Sunday and Monday bring the Caribbean trade winds, which blow offshore at Nosara, so those are the clean surf mornings. From Tuesday the marine forecast swings the wind onshore from the west and northwest. The low the hurricane center is watching has shifted west toward Mexico, well away from us. Multi-day soaking rain stays watch-only, and Oct 15–19 is the stretch to keep an eye on.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Sat–Mon, Oct 10–12)
periods.pattern: Tropical wave #50 crosses the country today. Costa Rica's weather service expects partly cloudy skies early, possible showers on the Pacific side before noon, then a big jump in downpours and thunderstorms this afternoon. Tonight the rain stays mostly over the North Pacific, the Northern Zone and the Central Valley. Model averages put roughly a quarter to three-quarters of an inch (about 10–20 mm) on the Nicoya Peninsula through tonight, and storms can drop more in spots. The Caribbean trades fill in behind the wave Sunday and peak Monday. That usually means a drier Pacific side, with the clouds and rain piled up on the Caribbean slope.
periods.implications: Get outdoor stuff done this morning. Plan to be under cover from mid-afternoon into the evening, and watch creeks and low roads, since the ground is already wet. Sunday may start with leftover showers but should dry out. Monday looks like the cleanest, least stormy day on our side.
periods.confidence: High on a stormy Saturday afternoon and evening and on the trades Sunday into Monday. Moderate on how much rain falls right at Nosara.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Tue–Fri, Oct 13–16)
periods.pattern: The trades ease Tuesday, and every model has light, variable wind over Costa Rica by Wednesday through Friday. The marine forecast goes northwest Tuesday, then west to southwest into Wednesday night, so Pacific air takes over. Both U.S. models now show a weak low in the western Caribbean near Nicaragua and Panama around Thursday, Oct 15. That could keep winds light and pull Pacific moisture onto our coast. The European models are quieter and keep rain light to moderate.
periods.implications: Expect the usual October rhythm: decent mornings, then a higher chance of afternoon and evening storms than Sunday or Monday. Rain stays hit-or-miss day to day, not a washout.
periods.confidence: Moderate on light winds and a return of afternoon storms. Low to moderate on the Caribbean low and how much it matters for us.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Sat–Sat, Oct 17–24)
periods.pattern: The models still don't agree. The U.S. ensemble is broadly wetter over Costa Rica and the nearby Pacific Oct 18–19. The standard European ensemble puts a wetter patch just off the Nicoya coast around Oct 18. The European AI ensemble keeps the heavier rain on the Caribbean side and the Pacific drier. After about Oct 19, all three ensembles bring easterly trades back across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica through Oct 22, which would favor a drier Pacific side again. Costa Rica's long-range outlook still calls for below-normal rain. For the North Pacific it expects about 5–90 mm (up to roughly 3.5 inches) for the week of Oct 12–18 and 1–70 mm for Oct 19–25, then very dry from about Oct 26.
periods.implications: Still leans drier than a normal October. Keep Oct 17–19 flexible for anything rain-sensitive, and look for the trades and better weather to return around Oct 20–22.
periods.confidence: Low to moderate. The models split on how wet our coast gets around Oct 18.

surfWinds.regime: Today is mixed, with a light northeast flow from Papagayo and southwest just to our south, plus storm outflow this afternoon. Sunday and Monday turn to Caribbean trades, offshore at Nosara. From Monday night into Wednesday it shifts to Pacific flow (south, then northwest to west), which is onshore and choppy.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 12:50 a.m. PDT Saturday) has northeast wind around 10 knots today and northeast to east 10 knots tonight. The zone just south of us, central and southern Costa Rica, has southwest 10 knots, and Nosara sits near the boundary. So expect a light, offshore-leaning early morning before the sea breeze and storm gusts take over. Sunday and Sunday night are east to southeast 10–15 knots, and Monday is east 10–15 knots. That's the real Caribbean trade, offshore to side-offshore here. Monday night turns south around 10 knots, which is side-onshore. Tuesday is northwest 10–15 knots, Tuesday night west 10 knots, and Wednesday west to northwest, then southwest to west. All of that is onshore and choppy. Seas are 4–6 feet from the south-southwest with long 15–17 second periods through Wednesday. That's a touch smaller than yesterday's 5–7 feet for Monday in our zone. Nicaragua: every model blows the trades across Nicaragua and out over the Pacific Sunday through Tuesday, so Nicaragua likely goes all-day offshore Sunday and Monday. That's a good sign for strong, clean Nosara mornings, but it doesn't mean all-day offshore here. The ensembles bring those Nicaragua trades back around Oct 19–22.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today, go at dawn before the sea breeze and the storms. Sunday morning through Monday morning (Oct 11–12) is the best offshore window, and Sunday and Monday could hold clean well past breakfast. Tuesday and Wednesday look onshore, so if you go, go very early and expect texture. Next possible offshore stretch is around Oct 19–22, low confidence.
surfWinds.confidence: High on trades Sunday into Monday. Moderate on the onshore turn Tuesday and Wednesday. Low beyond Oct 17.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, nothing established. Slightly lower than yesterday, now that the hurricane center's low has shifted toward Mexico.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Oct 15–19, mainly from the U.S. models, with the wettest area just offshore.
gyreWatch.supporting: Both U.S. models now show a weak low in the western Caribbean around Oct 15, with light winds over Costa Rica. That setup can let Pacific moisture pile onto our coast for several days. The U.S. ensemble is broadly wetter over Costa Rica and the nearby Pacific Oct 18–19. The standard European ensemble shows a wetter patch just off Nicoya around Oct 18. The marine forecast turns the wind west to southwest Tuesday and Wednesday, which brings Pacific air onshore.
gyreWatch.conflicting: The hurricane center now expects its low to form south or southwest of Mexico (70% within a week), well west of Central America, so it won't draw a big monsoon flow toward us. The European AI ensemble keeps the heavier rain on the Caribbean side. All three ensembles bring the easterly trades back across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica around Oct 19–22. Costa Rica's long-range outlook calls for below-normal rain through Oct 25 and a very dry North Pacific from about Oct 26. The U.S. tropics outlook (Oct 6) expects below-normal Caribbean rain and doesn't flag a Central American gyre.

whatChanged: The tropical wave arrives today, Saturday daytime, instead of Saturday night. Costa Rica's weather service put out an alert Friday afternoon about strong storms and saturated soils in the North Pacific. Nicoya's high is about 34°C, down from 36°C. The hurricane center's low moved west, from south of Guatemala to south or southwest of Mexico, at 70% (up from 60%) and farther from us. The marine forecast now turns onshore Tuesday and Wednesday (northwest to west), where yesterday Tuesday still looked possibly clean. Sunday's trade went up to east-southeast 10–15 knots (from about 10). Our zone's swell holds at 4–6 feet, with the 5–7 foot Monday pulse now only to the north. New: both U.S. models show a weak western Caribbean low around Oct 15, and the watch window moves up to Oct 15–19 (from Oct 16–20).
practical: Do outdoor plans and errands this morning, and expect thunderstorms this afternoon and evening. Avoid flooded crossings, because the ground is saturated. Surf at dawn today, then circle Sunday and Monday mornings (Oct 11–12) for clean offshore surf with long-period south-southwest swell. Expect onshore wind Tuesday and Wednesday. Keep Oct 17–19 flexible. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
